    word_document: default

# Make sure the data file "Tech-Sales-Reps.csv" and the R codes "Lab-2 R Codes.Rmd" are stored in the same folder.

# Step 1: Import the dataset "Tech-Sales-Reps.csv" to RStudio

```{r}

rm(list = ls())   # clean the working environment

# Import the data set into RStudio (data frame).
mydata <- read.csv("Tech_Sales_Reps.csv")

# Produce the summary measures to get a picture of the data set.
summary(mydata) 

```

# Step 2: Calculate some basic descriptive statistics for variable NPS (net promoter score).  
# Note: We reference the variable:  "Dataframe$Variable"

```{r}

meanNPS <- mean (mydata$NPS) # Calculate the mean of NPS.
meanNPS

medianNPS <-median (mydata$NPS) # Calculate the median of NPS.
medianNPS

varianceNPS <-var (mydata$NPS) # Calculate the variance of NPS.
varianceNPS

StdDevNPS <-sd (mydata$NPS) # Calculate the standard deviation of NPS.
StdDevNPS

iqrNPS <- IQR (mydata$NPS) # Calculate the Inter-Quartile Range of NPS.
iqrNPS

```

# Step 3: Create a simple boxplot and histogram of variable NPS.

```{r}
boxplot(mydata$NPS)

```

# Now, make the boxplot nicer by adding labels to the boxplot, making it "horizontal" and  coloring the box "gold".  

```{r}

boxplot (mydata$NPS, main = "Tech Sales Reps: Net Promoter Score", xlab = "NPS Score", horizontal = TRUE, col = "gold")

```

# Step 4: Use the  tapply() function to tabulate/calculate the average NPS score for four different types of Personality.

```{r}

tapply (mydata$NPS, mydata$Personality, mean)

```

# Conclusion: The sales representatives with the personalities of Diplomat and Explorer have higher customer satisfaction and loyalty (as reflected by the NPS scores).

# Step 5: You can also do the cross tabulation (two-way table) for the average NPS score using: four "Personality" types and "Business" (Hardware or Software).


```{r}

print ("Cross-tabulation for average NPS scores")

tapply (mydata$NPS , list(mydata$Personality, mydata$Business) , mean)

```
